title: The bootstrap engine: directory guard, git init, scaffold write, first commit, the gh port and the receipt
description:
SPIDR child of task-facff1d1e7ce44a6b1101490524890a9 (architect-fa3a3e17, 2026-09-05), which measured over the file cap. dependsOn task-4a0f706437a042059789be2ebdb98bc0 for the scaffold tree it writes.

WHY THIS ROW EXISTS. The parent owns `repository.bootstrap` end to end. Publishing ONE command kind on this board costs 13 forced edits on its own (measured below), so the parent cannot also carry the engine, the ports and the receipt inside a 10-file plan. This row is the dependency LEAF: the whole bootstrap sequence as a pure, injectable, offline-testable service, plus the handler entry point the parent will register. NO command kind, NO vocabulary edit, NO registry edit, NO MCP roster edit - all of that is the parent.

MEASURED AT HEAD (branch moe/work-2026-09-04) by architect-fa3a3e17:
- `git grep -rc 'repo create' apps/ tools/` = 0. No GitHub repository creation path exists.
- `apps/daemon/src/repository/git-landing-port.ts:68` already exports an injectable `GitRunner` type and `nodeGitRunner` (spawn-based, 243 lines). It handles add/commit/push but NOT `init`. REUSE the `GitRunner` seam; do not write a second process launcher.
- `apps/daemon/src/repository/landing-receipt-contracts.ts` (236 lines) is the receipt shape to mirror.
- `project.bind_repository` is real and is handled at `apps/daemon/src/bootstrap/bootstrap-services.ts:227` (`bindRepository`), with `apps/daemon/src/bootstrap/bootstrap-sequence.ts:36` requiring `project.register` FIRST. That ordering is a real constraint on this row's sequence.
- The "manager catalog" the parent's DoD names is `apps/daemon/src/projects/project-catalog.ts` - it exists.
- Every new `.ts` under apps/daemon needs a tracked one-line `.js` bridge (`export * from "./x.ts";`). Budget two files per module.

GITHUB IS OPTIONAL AND THAT IS LOAD-BEARING. A local-only bootstrap SUCCEEDS and says so: `gh` absent refuses BOOTSTRAP_GH_UNAVAILABLE for the GitHub half ONLY, while the local repository still exists, is committed and is bound, and the receipt records remoteUrl: null. Failing the whole bootstrap because `gh` is missing would make the feature unusable on most machines.

THE DIRECTORY GUARD IS THE SAFETY PROPERTY. This command writes a whole tree at an operator-supplied path. BOOTSTRAP_DIR_NOT_EMPTY must refuse BEFORE anything is written.
definitionOfDone: The four refusal codes are defined here with their layer and are each asserted with CODE AND LAYER, never merely `ok:false`: BOOTSTRAP_DIR_NOT_EMPTY, BOOTSTRAP_GIT_UNAVAILABLE, BOOTSTRAP_GH_UNAVAILABLE, BOOTSTRAP_PROFILE_VERSION_UNKNOWN (the last one re-exported from child 1's generator, not redefined). Reuse an already-rostered layer literal; introduce no new `*_LAYER` constant.

BOOTSTRAP_DIR_NOT_EMPTY is asserted against a real temp directory containing exactly ONE file, and the test asserts NOTHING WAS WRITTEN - read the directory back and assert its entries are unchanged. Also assert a non-existent directory IS created and an EMPTY existing one IS accepted. This is the safety property of the row, so mutate the guard and confirm the arm goes red.

A local-only bootstrap through the service SUCCEEDS with the gh port reporting absent: the temp directory is a git repository, `git log --oneline` is exactly ONE line reading `chore: scaffold by Moe`, and the result carries BOOTSTRAPPED with remoteUrl: null plus the code BOOTSTRAP_GH_UNAVAILABLE for the GitHub half. Assert all of it.

GitHub creation is tested OFFLINE through an injectable port that captures argv, asserting the `gh` argv BYTE-FOR-BYTE as `["repo","create","<owner>/<name>","--<visibility>","--source",".","--push"]`. No network call in any test, no stored token, no REST fallback.

`moe-bootstrap-receipt/1` is defined mirroring apps/daemon/src/repository/landing-receipt-contracts.ts and records {dir, sha, remoteUrl|null, BOOTSTRAPPED|REFUSED(code)}; a REFUSED receipt carries its code and NO sha, and that is asserted as its own arm.

The service reuses the EXISTING `GitRunner` seam from apps/daemon/src/repository/git-landing-port.ts and the EXISTING bind path (`bindRepository` in apps/daemon/src/bootstrap/bootstrap-services.ts, after `project.register` per bootstrap-sequence.ts:36). A second process launcher or a second binding path is a rejection. Name the reuse with a grep -n in the completion record.

EVERY temp directory and child process the tests create is removed on EVERY exit path including the throwing one (epic rail 4) - teardown in a `finally`, not after the assertions. Invoke `git`/`gh` as bare executables under shell:false with argv arrays; never a hard-coded `.cmd`, never a shell string, never a chain.

Gates quoted with their `Test Files N passed` count lines: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, `pnpm typecheck`. Root `pnpm test` does NOT cover apps/**, so the daemon leg is the only apps/** evidence - say so rather than quoting a bare root count line.
taskRails: NO COMMAND KIND. No edit to daemon-command-vocabulary.ts, daemon-command-registry.ts, mcp-tool-allowlist.ts, agent-spawn-contract.ts, or packages/contracts - every one of those belongs to the parent task-facff1d1e7ce44a6b1101490524890a9 and touching them here collides in the shared worktree.
NEVER WRITE INTO A NON-EMPTY DIRECTORY. The guard refuses before the first byte is written, not after.
A LOCAL-ONLY BOOTSTRAP IS A SUCCESS. `gh` absent refuses only the GitHub half.
REUSE the GitRunner seam and the existing bind path. A second launcher or a second binding path defeats the row.
`gh` CLI ONLY, matching the Gate 3 decision (task-f961dc89): no stored token, no REST fallback.
OFFLINE TESTS ONLY. Every port is injectable; no test may reach the network.

implementationPlan.description:
CONTRACTS: refusal codes, the receipt, the request/result types, and the port interfaces. Create `repository-bootstrap-contracts.ts` (+ one-line `.js` bridge).

REFUSAL CODES — all four as `as const` string literals, each paired with an ALREADY-ROSTERED layer literal. Use `"DAEMON_INGRESS"`, which bootstrap-services.ts:100 already uses in `refuse(request.kind, "BOOTSTRAP_PAYLOAD_INVALID", "DAEMON_INGRESS")`. Introduce NO new `*_LAYER` constant — the security lane carries a boundary roster over those and a new one demands a backfill this row does not own.
- `BOOTSTRAP_DIR_NOT_EMPTY`, `BOOTSTRAP_GIT_UNAVAILABLE`, `BOOTSTRAP_GH_UNAVAILABLE` defined here.
- `BOOTSTRAP_PROFILE_VERSION_UNKNOWN` RE-EXPORTED from child 1's generator module, never redefined. Two definitions of one code is exactly the drift the code exists to prevent.

RECEIPT — mirror apps/daemon/src/repository/landing-receipt-contracts.ts: `BOOTSTRAP_RECEIPT_VERSION = "moe-bootstrap-receipt/1" as const` and `BootstrapReceiptV1 { dir; sha: string | null; remoteUrl: string | null; outcome: "BOOTSTRAPPED" | "REFUSED"; refusal: { code; detail } | null; decidedAt; version }`. Follow the landing receipt's null-pairing discipline: the success member and the refusal member are both nullable and EXACTLY ONE is populated — a REFUSED receipt carries its code and NO sha, and that invariant is asserted in step 7.

PORTS — declare, do not implement: a `GhRunner` reusing the EXISTING `GitRunner` type shape from git-landing-port.ts:68 (`(cwd, args, stdin?) => Promise<{code, stderr, stdout}>`) but distinguishing EXECUTABLE-ABSENT from nonzero-exit; a `TreeWriterPort`; a `RepositoryBoundPort` and a `CatalogRegistrationPort` that the PARENT row supplies from the existing `bindRepository` (bootstrap-services.ts:96) and `project-catalog.ts`. This row calls those two, never implements them.

A SECRET NEVER SURFACES (epic rail 3): the receipt's `remoteUrl` and every refusal `detail` are shaped so a token embedded in a remote URL cannot be stored or printed. Say in a comment how that is enforced.
implementationPlan.note: Contracts + bridge delivered with discriminated receipt null-pair and DAEMON_INGRESS provenance. githubRefusal is separate from local refusal so optional GH failure cannot violate success sha/refusal invariant. Diagnostics are closed literals; service will admit only canonical GitHub URLs. Parent-supplied bind port explicitly requires prior durable project.register and must throw on refusal. Planned test file created early for TDD: missing constants RED (1 failed), then GREEN Test Files 1 passed (1), Tests 1 passed (1). No package edge: imports are intra-daemon. implementationPlan.description:
HOST PORTS. Create `repository-bootstrap-ports.ts` (+ bridge) with the production implementations only — no sequencing logic.

GIT: reuse `nodeGitRunner` and `landingEnvironment()` from git-landing-port.ts rather than writing a second launcher. `landingEnvironment()` strips every `GIT_*` variable from the parent environment — a parent shell's `GIT_DIR` / `GIT_WORK_TREE` / `GIT_INDEX_FILE` would silently redirect `git init` into the WRONG repository, which in this row means writing a product tree into someone else's checkout. That hygiene is not optional here. If the function is not exported, export it in this step rather than copying it.
- `git init` in the target directory; `git add -A` scoped to that directory; `git -c user.name=Moe -c user.email=moe@moe.local -c commit.gpgsign=false commit -m "chore: scaffold by Moe"` reusing the existing `LANDER_IDENTITY` array. The identity is Moe's, never the operator's, so the first commit does not depend on the operator having git configured at all.
- Spawn failure (ENOENT) => `BOOTSTRAP_GIT_UNAVAILABLE`.

GH: same discipline — bare executable `gh`, argv array, `shell: false`, `windowsHide: true`, an explicit timeout, no shell string, no `&&` chain, no pipe, and NEVER a hard-coded `gh.cmd` (the measured host returns EINVAL for a `.cmd` under `shell:false`). Argv is exactly `["repo","create","<owner>/<name>","--<visibility>","--source",".","--push"]`.
- DISTINGUISH TWO OUTCOMES, because collapsing them costs the diagnosis: spawn ENOENT means `gh` is ABSENT; a nonzero exit means GitHub refused. Both refuse only the GitHub half with `BOOTSTRAP_GH_UNAVAILABLE`, and the detail says which. No stored token, no REST fallback, no `GH_TOKEN` read.

TREE WRITER: write child 1's `ReadonlyMap<path, bytes>` under the target directory, creating parent directories. Reject any path that is absolute, contains a `..` segment, or resolves outside the target after normalization — the generator is trusted, but this writer is the last place a bad path can be stopped before bytes land at an operator-supplied root.
implementationPlan.note: Host ports reuse nodeGitRunner, newly exported existing LANDER_IDENTITY/landingEnvironment (only two export edits). Git first commit has verified SHA. GH injectable exec boundary bare gh, argv, shell:false/windowsHide/60s timeout; ENOENT distinct from exit 1; output discarded and remote derived. Tree checks all paths before any writes, guards files/junctions/dotfiles/UNC/empty input; rechecks prepare/write gap and uses wx. Tests written first from step-5 roster: initial export assertion RED then Test Files 1 passed (1), Tests 24 passed (24). Initial real-git tests exceeded default 5s (14s suite); explicitly bounded at 300s to permit process completion/finally cleanup. Confirmed zero remaining test temp directories and git processes after run. pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck exit 0.

implementationPlan.description:
THE SEQUENCE. Create `repository-bootstrap-service.ts` (+ bridge): a pure function over injected ports, returning a `BootstrapReceiptV1`. Order is load-bearing and each guard runs BEFORE anything is written:

1. PROFILE VERSION first — an unknown version refuses `BOOTSTRAP_PROFILE_VERSION_UNKNOWN` before any filesystem contact, so a typo cannot create a directory.
2. DIRECTORY GUARD second, and this is the safety property of the row: probe the target. Non-existent => create it and proceed. Exists and EMPTY => proceed. Exists with ANY entry => refuse `BOOTSTRAP_DIR_NOT_EMPTY` having written NOTHING. This command writes a whole tree at a path the operator typed; a wrong path that buries an existing directory is the worst outcome available here, so the refusal precedes the first byte, never follows it. Decide and document how a dotfile-only directory and a directory that is actually a FILE are answered.
3. Generate the tree via child 1's generator; write it.
4. `git init`, `git add`, first commit. Spawn failure => `BOOTSTRAP_GIT_UNAVAILABLE`. Capture the resulting sha.
5. GitHub half, ONLY if the caller asked for it. `gh` absent or failing => `BOOTSTRAP_GH_UNAVAILABLE` for THIS HALF ONLY — the receipt still records `BOOTSTRAPPED` with `remoteUrl: null` and carries the code in its detail. A LOCAL-ONLY BOOTSTRAP IS A SUCCESS: failing the whole operation because `gh` is missing would make the feature unusable on the majority of machines, and that inversion is the single most likely way this row regresses.
6. Hand off to `RepositoryBoundPort` then `CatalogRegistrationPort` — call them, never reimplement them.

The service performs no process spawning and no direct `fs` calls of its own; everything goes through the step-3 ports so every arm in step 6 runs offline.
implementationPlan.note: Sequence + bridge: version/name/GitHub validation before fs; tree prepare/write then reused Git port then optional GH then bind/catalog. Pure service has no fs/process calls. Returns honest failure receipt on effect throws; parent owns durable persistence and project.register-before-bind. Added service tests from planned steps 6/7 before implementation (missing export RED), then 2 files/39 tests GREEN; daemon typecheck exit 0 after fixing test literal widening. Validator moved within owned contracts/ports to keep service independent of host implementations. Added partial-commit and thrown-I/O arms; will rerun in next step.

implementationPlan.description:
HOST PORT TESTS — `repository-bootstrap-ports.test.ts`. These are the only arms that touch a real process, and they never touch the network.

- REAL GIT in a temp directory: init, add, commit with the Moe identity; then assert `git log --oneline` is EXACTLY ONE line reading `chore: scaffold by Moe`. Assert the LINE COUNT as well as the text — a substring match would pass on a two-commit history.
- Assert the commit's author is Moe, not the host's git config, by reading it back. This proves `LANDER_IDENTITY` was actually applied rather than inherited.
- Assert `landingEnvironment()` hygiene bites: set `GIT_DIR` in the child environment and confirm the init still lands in the target directory. This is the arm that catches a product tree being written into a foreign checkout.
- GH PORT, offline: assert spawn ENOENT maps to executable-absent and a nonzero exit maps to GitHub-refused, and that the two are DISTINGUISHABLE. Assert the argv is built byte-for-byte as `["repo","create","<owner>/<name>","--<visibility>","--source",".","--push"]`. No network call.
- TREE WRITER: an absolute path, a `..` segment, and a path that normalizes outside the target are each REFUSED and write nothing.

EVERY temp directory is removed in a `finally`, not after the assertions — a throwing arm must not leak (epic rail 4: a test that leaks makes every later gate on this board inadmissible). Every child process must exit or be killed before the arm returns; a held handle also reds unrelated suites on Windows.

implementationPlan.description:
SERVICE TESTS, PART 1 — the refusals, in `repository-bootstrap-service.test.ts`. Every arm asserts the CODE AND THE LAYER, never merely that it failed: a test asserting only "refused" is one added layer away from vacuous, because a second refusal layer can answer first and the arm stays green while no longer testing its subject.

(a) `BOOTSTRAP_DIR_NOT_EMPTY` — the safety arm. A real temp directory containing exactly ONE file. Assert code + layer, AND read the directory back and assert its entries are byte-identical to before: hash the existing file first and re-hash after. Proving NOTHING WAS WRITTEN is the point; an arm that only checks the return value would pass while the tree had already been laid down.
(b) A NON-EXISTENT directory IS created and accepted.
(c) An EMPTY existing directory IS accepted.
(d) `BOOTSTRAP_GIT_UNAVAILABLE` — git port reports absent; code + layer.
(e) `BOOTSTRAP_PROFILE_VERSION_UNKNOWN` — an unknown profile version; code + layer; and assert NO directory was created, which pins the step-4 ordering that puts the version check before any filesystem contact.
(f) PRECEDENCE: with BOTH an unknown version and a non-empty directory, assert WHICH code wins. An unpinned precedence is how these two arms silently start testing each other.

MUTATION CHECK for (a): invert the guard, confirm the arm goes RED, restore. Record the result — a failure-path test that has never been seen red is not evidence.

implementationPlan.description:
SERVICE TESTS, PART 2 — the success paths and the receipt, same file.

(g) LOCAL-ONLY SUCCESS with the gh port reporting ABSENT. Assert ALL of it: the outcome is `BOOTSTRAPPED`; `remoteUrl` is null; the receipt carries `BOOTSTRAP_GH_UNAVAILABLE` for the GitHub half; the directory is a git repository; the tree matches child 1's generated map; `git log --oneline` is exactly ONE line reading `chore: scaffold by Moe`; and the `RepositoryBoundPort` and `CatalogRegistrationPort` doubles each received exactly one call with the expected arguments. A bootstrap that fails wholesale without `gh` is unusable on most machines — this arm is the regression fence for that inversion, so make it explicit rather than folding it into a generic happy path.
(h) GITHUB HALF REQUESTED AND AVAILABLE, offline through the argv-capturing double: the captured argv is asserted byte-for-byte, and the receipt records the remote URL. No network.
(i) GITHUB HALF FAILS (nonzero exit, not absent): the LOCAL repository still exists, is committed and is handed to the bind port; the receipt is still `BOOTSTRAPPED` with `remoteUrl: null`, and the detail distinguishes refused-by-GitHub from gh-absent.
(j) RECEIPT INVARIANT, its own arm: a REFUSED receipt carries its code and `sha: null`; a BOOTSTRAPPED receipt carries a sha and `refusal: null`. Assert both directions — exactly one member populated — mirroring the null-pairing in landing-receipt-contracts.ts.
(k) NO SECRET SURFACES (epic rail 3): drive the gh port with a remote URL carrying an embedded credential and assert it appears in NEITHER the receipt NOR any refusal detail.

Teardown for every temp directory in a `finally`.

ADVERSARIAL SELF-REVIEW before `moe.complete_task`.

THE DIRECTORY GUARD IS THE ATTACK SURFACE — answer each with a command:
- What does the guard do when the target is a FILE, a symlink to a non-empty directory, a path with a trailing separator, an empty string, a UNC path, or a directory containing only dotfiles? Each needs a defined answer, and "it threw" is not one.
- Does the probe-then-write sequence have a window? If the directory becomes non-empty between the probe and the write, what happens? Say which, and whether it matters at this trust level.
- Run the whole thing TWICE against the same directory: the second run must refuse `BOOTSTRAP_DIR_NOT_EMPTY`, not append a second commit. Assert it.
- Does the tree writer stop a path that escapes the target? You wrote the check in step 3 — confirm the arm actually reds when you remove it.

PARTIAL-FAILURE HONESTY:
- If `git init` succeeds and the commit fails, what is on disk and what does the receipt say? A REFUSED receipt with no sha over a directory that now holds a tree is a real state — document it rather than pretending it cannot happen, and say whether a retry can describe it.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
WHERE THE BINDING AND THE CATALOG LIVE. Considered doing bind + catalog registration inside this service. REJECTED: `bindRepository` is a `CommandHandler` that needs a command `context` and `reduceAndCommit`, which only exists at the dispatch edge — pulling it in here would drag the command context into a pure service and put this row back over its file budget. This row declares narrow port interfaces (`RepositoryBoundPort`, `CatalogRegistrationPort`) and the PARENT supplies implementations backed by the existing `bindRepository` and `project-catalog.ts`. That satisfies "reuse, do not reinvent" — the test for it is that no second binding implementation exists anywhere, which is a grep, not a call.

WHETHER TO WRITE A SECOND PROCESS LAUNCHER FOR `gh`. Rejected. `GitRunner`'s shape `(cwd, args, stdin?) => Promise<{code, stderr, stdout}>` is executable-agnostic; the gh port reuses the same TYPE with a different executable, so one discipline covers both and the argv-capture double in the tests is one implementation.

HOW `gh` ABSENCE IS DETECTED. Considered probing with `gh --version` first. REJECTED as a second failure mode: a probe that succeeds and a create that then fails leaves two paths to BOOTSTRAP_GH_UNAVAILABLE. Instead the port reports absence as a distinct outcome from a nonzero exit — ENOENT from the spawn is `gh` absent (BOOTSTRAP_GH_UNAVAILABLE), a nonzero exit is a GitHub-side failure. Both refuse only the GitHub half; the local repository stands either way. State which is which in the receipt detail.

SPLITTING THIS ROW FURTHER. Not needed: 8 files, 9 steps, both inside the thresholds.
